prompt_meta.title: CorePlumb — plumbing & handyman marketing site (faithful rebuild of a Framer template)
prompt_meta.objective: Recreate the reference website as a production-quality Next.js site that matches its layout, spacing, typography, colors, components, responsive behavior, animations and interactions as closely as possible. This JSON is the full spec. Open the reference URL in the Antigravity browser to compare.
fidelity_rules: Match the reference at 1440px (desktop), 1000px (tablet) and 390px (mobile) widths; the breakpoints are desktop >=1200px, tablet 810-1199.98px, mobile <=809.98px.
Use the exact values in design_system and motion_system. Where a value is marked "estimated", confirm it against the live reference in the browser.
Do not add sections, content, or features that are not in the reference. Do not "improve" the design.
Do NOT recreate the Framer promo overlays ("Get this Template for free" pill bottom-left, "Made in Framer" badge bottom-right) — they are not part of the design.

Short UI copy in this spec is final copy — use it verbatim. Where the spec says a block is long-form (FAQ answers, blog bodies, service detail body, privacy policy), write ORIGINAL copy that follows the given outline, length and topic.
Images: generate or source original photos matching each image_assets entry (subject, aspect ratio, treatment). Never hotlink the reference site's assets.
Every animation and interaction listed in motion_system must be implemented and must respect prefers-reduced-motion (the reference ignores it; honoring it is an intentional accessibility addition).

Also fix the service-card typo "ast drain cleaning" → "Fast clearing…" wording as given in cms_data, and in the home FAQ make sure each answer matches its question (the reference has the answers to questions 3 and 4 swapped).
reconciled_notes: Testimonials marquee: two rows, opposite directions, ~10px/s, 24px gap, edge fade mask; on hover the speed drops to 90% (hoverFactor 0.9), it does NOT pause. Draggable only on touch/mobile.

Reveal system is intentionally simple: hero elements fade-up on page load (opacity 0→1, y 24→0, 0.55s, ease [0.44,0,0.56,1]); every other block fades-up once when 20% in view (y 28→0, same timing). No stagger, parallax, counters, page transitions, or smooth-scroll library (only CSS smooth scrolling for anchor links).
Where a value is marked "estimated" or an icon is a "closest match", verify it in the browser against the reference before finalizing.

agent_instructions.role: You are a senior front-end engineer and motion designer rebuilding a reference website with pixel-level fidelity.
working_style: 1. Read this whole spec first. Produce a short implementation plan artifact (routes, components, data files) before writing code.
2. Scaffold the project (tech_stack) and encode design_system as Tailwind theme + CSS variables, fonts via next/font.
3. Build motion primitives (lib/motion.ts presets + <Reveal>, <Stagger>, <Marquee>, <CursorFollower>, <Accordion>) from motion_system before building sections.
4. Build global_components (Header, MobileMenu, Footer, Button, TrustBadge, SectionHeading), then pages section by section in the listed order.
5. Add cms_data as typed local data files and generate the dynamic routes with generateStaticParams.

6. Verify: run the dev server, open both your build and the reference URL in the browser at 1440/1000/390, screenshot each section side by side, list the differences, fix them. Do at least 2 comparison passes per page.
7. Finish with the acceptance_criteria checklist and report any deviations.
deliverables: Working Next.js project that runs with `npm install && npm run dev` and builds with `npm run build` without errors or type errors.
All routes listed in reference_pages, including a custom 404.
Generated/placeholder images saved under public/images with descriptive filenames.
README.md explaining how to edit brand facts, services, posts, and FAQs.

tech_stack.animation: motion (the framer-motion package, import from "motion/react"). Reason: the reference was built in Framer, whose animations are framer-motion configs, so the spring/tween values in motion_system map 1:1.
tech_stack.icons: lucide-react (primary) + @phosphor-icons/react where the spec names a Phosphor icon
tech_stack.fonts: next/font/google (see design_system.typography for families and fallbacks)
tech_stack.forms: Client-side only: controlled inputs, simple validation (required fields, email format), a success toast/inline message on submit. No backend; leave a clearly marked TODO for wiring to an API/Formspree.
tech_stack.content: Typed local data in /data (services.ts, posts.ts, testimonials.ts, faqs.ts, team.ts). Blog/service bodies as MDX or structured arrays of blocks.
tech_stack.seo: Next.js Metadata API per route, sitemap.ts, robots.ts, JSON-LD (Plumber/LocalBusiness, FAQPage, BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList).
tech_stack.quality: ESLint + Prettier; no console errors; images via next/image with explicit sizes.
tech_stack.alternative_stack_note: If a framework is not wanted: static multi-page HTML + Tailwind (CDN or CLI) + Motion One / GSAP ScrollTrigger. Keep the same tokens, presets and timings from this spec.

notes: The site's motion system is small and consistent: one load-appear (hero), one in-view section reveal, plus variant-driven hover/press on components. There is no parallax, no scroll-linked transforms, no counters, no per-child stagger and no page transitions.
